Register KVM's cpuhp and syscore callback when enabling virtualization
in hardware instead of registering the callbacks during initialization
and let the CPU up/down framework invoke the inner enable/disable
functions.  Registering the callbacks during initialization makes things
more complex than they need to be
column2: as KVM needs to be very careful about

column1: handling races between enabling CPUs being onlined/offlined and hardware
being enabled/disabled.
Intel TDX support will require KVM to enable virtualization during KVM
initialization
column2: i.e. will add another wrinkle to things

column1: sorting out the potential races with kvm_usage_count would become even
more complex.
Note
column2: using the cpuhp framework has a subtle behavioral change: enabling

column1: will be done serially across all CPUs
column2: whereas KVM currently sends an IPI

column1: to all CPUs in parallel.  While serializing virtualization enabling could
create undesirable latency
column2: the issue is limited to the 0=>1 transition of

column1: VM creation.  And even that can be mitigated
force virtualization to be enabled when KVM is initialized.
